newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar firmer on overseas cross buying.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar firmer on overseas cross buying.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3626 (US$0.7338) in light trading after continuing to rally last night on overseas markets, traders said. * They said the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady combined with cross-buying sentiment against the Japanese yen and German mark to underpin the Canada dollar.
"The stage has been set for a radically stronger Canadian dollar," one trader said.
The Canadian dollar has been under pressure from investors since the Federal Reserve raised interest rates on March 25 and the Bank of Canada held its own rates steady.

The possibility of the Bank of Canada resisting another Fed hike had raised the specter of a widening in the spread between U.S. and Canadian interest rates and a consequent sell-off of the Canada dollar.
Analysts said relieved markets now would refocus attention on daily U.S. and Canadian economic data ahead of July 1.

Statistics Canada reported on Wednesday that retail sales fell 0.8 percent in March after a 1.1 percent increase in February. Meanwhile, Canada's merchandise trade surplus jumped to C$2.45 billion in March from February's revised figure of C$2.19 billion, Statistics Canada said.
"Those numbers are disappointing, but they should be generally neutral for the Canadian dollar," said Steve Saldanha, economist with Canada Trust.
"I think we can eventually touch C$1.3500 (US$0.7407), but I wouldn't look for a breakout until after the Canadian election on June 2," Saldanha added.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 83.45 yen from Tuesday's close of 82.34 and jumped to 1.2395 marks from Tuesday's 1.2263 marks.
